newsitem.title: JAPAN: DDI hits record parent profit, but group in red.
newsitem.headline: DDI hits record parent profit, but group in red.

text.p: Japan's second-largest telephone operator DDI Corp on Thursday unveiled a record parent profit last year thanks to fast-growing domestic telecom demand, but plunged into the red on a group basis.
The operator of domestic long-distance telecom services said its parent current profit grew 17.4 percent to a record 67.76 billion yen ($584 million) in the year to March 31.
A recent cut in the access charges DDI pays to Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) for use of NTT facilities also contributed to the the profit.

On a group basis, however, DDI suffered a net loss of 26.16 billion yen ($225 million) in 1996/97, depressed by a hefty loss incurred in its personal handyphone (PHS) units. It posted a profit of 4.28 billion yen ($36.8 million) in 1995/96.
Net profit is equal to current profit, which is pre-tax, minus taxes and extraordinary profits and losses.
By trimming sales promotion fees, DDI said it hopes to cut total net loss at its nine PHS units to ten billion yen this business year from 79.1 billion yen ($681 million) the previous year.
PHS is a a simplified, less-expensive type of cellular phone, started by DDI in July 1995.
DDI said its group would return to profit this year, helped by a smaller loss at the PHS units. It saw a group net profit of 29 billion yen ($250 million) for 1997/98.
Still, the figure was smaller than earlier estimates by analysts of around 45 billion yen ($387 million).

Analysts said high cancellation rates for the lower-tier service and still-expensive access charges paid to NTT for using its local networks would keep the division in the red this year, although the loss could be trimmed sharply.

DDI sees its accumulated subscribers rising to 15.5 million by March 1998, while its cellular units' subscribers were seen rising to 4.5 million and PHS units' subscribers to 4.2 million. (1$=116 yen)
